decisions.rationale: 'G6PD Nagano' names a newly described enzyme variant (a protein/gene variant of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase), not a disease entity, so it does not meet the disease-mention criterion.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (disease mention criterion: Specific Disease or Disease Class only)

decisions.rationale: 'Congenital hemolytic anemia' is a family of multiple inherited hemolytic anemias (e.g., G6PD deficiency, spherocytosis) and cannot be tied to one specific definition, so it is a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Disease Class definition); Examples §10-11

decisions.rationale: 'Chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia' is a grouping of several anemias sharing a clinical pattern rather than one specific disease, so it is a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Disease Class definition); Examples §11 (grey-area terms)

decisions.rationale: 'G6PD deficiency' refers to one specific enzyme-deficiency disease with a single definition, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease definition); Examples §6

decisions.rationale: 'Hemolytic crisis' denotes a discrete, named acute pathological episode of hemolysis in G6PD deficiency, a recognized clinical condition rather than a general term, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease definition); What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms excluded)

decisions.rationale: 'Upper respiratory infection' is a family of multiple distinct infections (e.g., pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis) rather than one specific disease, so it is a Disease Class.
This is a second occurrence of 'G6PD Nagano' in the abstract body, referring to the same enzyme variant rather than a disease, so it is not annotated, consistent with decision for id 1.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (disease mention criterion); What to Annotate §4 (duplicate mentions treated consistently)

decisions.rationale: 'Infection-induced hemolysis' describes a pathological process (red cell destruction) rather than a named disease entity; references to biological processes are excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §5 (references to biological processes)

decisions.rationale: 'Chronic hemolytic anemia' is a broad family of anemias with multiple possible causes and is not one specific disease, so it is a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Disease Class definition); Examples §10-11
